setup.zh: 褚先生讲灵根：一门者，气如江河；五门者，气如漏勺。满堂哄笑。「沈小满。你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
setup.en: Master Chu lectures on roots: one door, and the qi comes like a river; five doors, and it runs off like a skimmer. The hall roars. "Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

recap.zh: 褚先生当堂问你：漏勺能打水吗？你说：能，多打几次。
recap.en: Master Chu asked you before the whole hall whether a skimmer can carry water. You said: yes — go back for more.

zh: 褚先生讲灵根，山羊胡子一翘。
en: Master Chu lectures on roots; his goat's beard jerks.
"Five doors — a mixed root: the qi runs off like a skimmer."
"Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer carry water?"

text.zh: 胡子一翘一翘，倒像在替他点头；你暗暗数了，他讲一段，要翘七回。
text.en: The goatee bobs up and down as if nodding for him. You count on the quiet: seven bobs to a passage.

text.zh: 戒尺一头磨得发亮，另一头却新得很——先生打人，只用一头。
text.en: One end of the ruler is worn bright; the other looks new. The master only ever strikes with one end.

story.zh:
外门每日辰时上课，讲课的是褚先生，五十来岁，生得精瘦，颏下一撮山羊胡子，在外门讲了三十年经。讲堂是一间大屋，前头几排坐的是真灵根，后头几排坐的是杂灵根，这是谁也没定过的规矩，可谁都照着坐。小满坐在最后一排，孙二狗坐在他左边，马小宝凭着荐书，坐在第一排。

褚先生背着手，摇头晃脑地讲道：「天地之间，灵气充盈。凡人不能纳，修士能纳。何也？——灵根也。一门者，天灵根，气如江河；三门者，真灵根，气如沟渠；五门者——」山羊胡子一翘，目光不偏不倚停在小满身上，「——杂灵根，四面漏风，气如漏勺。」满堂登时哄笑起来。褚先生叫道：「沈小满。你说，漏勺能打水吗？」
story.en:
In the outer court, lessons began each day at the hour of Chen, and the one who lectured was Master Chu — fifty or so, lean, a tuft of goat's beard on his chin; he had lectured in the outer court for thirty years. The lecture hall was one big room; the true roots sat in front and the mixed roots at the back — nobody had ever made it a rule, and everybody kept it. Xiaoman sat in the back row with Sun Ergou on his left; Ma Xiaobao, on the strength of his letter, sat in the front.

Master Chu, hands behind his back, wagged his head and lectured: "Between heaven and earth, spirit qi is everywhere. Ordinary men cannot take it in; cultivators can. Why? — Spirit roots. One gate: a heavenly root, qi like a great river; three gates: a true root, qi like a canal; five gates —" the goat's beard tilted up, and his eyes came to rest, neither left nor right, on Xiaoman, "— a mixed root, wind leaking from every side, qi like a skimmer." The whole hall roared. Master Chu called, "Shen Xiaoman. Tell me — can a skimmer draw water?"

exits.means: answers that a skimmer can carry water — by going back more times

story.zh:
小满说：「能。」

满堂都是一愣，褚先生也愣了，半晌才道：「……怎么打？」

小满说：「多打几次。」

满堂又笑了，只是这一回笑的方向，跟方才有点不一样：前头几排回过头来瞧他，像瞧一个说胡话的傻子；后头几排的杂灵根们却不回头，一个个低着头，肩膀一抽一抽的。小满坐下，胸口的木牌忽地一烫，一个又困又不耐烦的声音在他耳朵里道：「……谁在吵？」他压低了头：「先生说杂灵根是漏勺。」那声音哼了一声：「他懂个屁。」木牌便凉了。小满拿袖子挡住了嘴，憋得两边肩膀直抖。孙二狗还道他是给骂哭了，悄悄在他背上拍了两下，小声道：「不怕。我是漏勺底下那个洞。」

褚先生却不肯放过那四个字。他把戒尺在讲桌上一敲：「多打几次？《列子》上有个愚公，快九十岁了，嫌两座大山挡了家门，带着儿孙一筐一筐挑土。有个聪明的老头叫智叟，笑话他连山上一根草都拔不动。诸位，智叟说得对不对？」前头几排齐声道：「对！」褚先生道：「所以做事，要先量力。漏勺，便是漏勺。」

后排一只手举了起来。小满站起来，道：「先生，后来呢？那个愚公，后来把山挖平了没有？」

褚先生的胡子不翘了。这个故事的后头，他自然是知道的：愚公说，我死了，还有儿子，儿子又生孙子，子子孙孙没有穷尽，山却不会再长高；天帝感他的诚，派两个大力神，把山背走了。他照本念完了，念得格外快，道：「……所以，是神仙帮忙。」小满道：「那也得先挖。他要是不挖，神仙上哪儿知道去？」

堂上没有人笑。褚先生站了好一会儿，道：「……今日便讲到这里。」那是他三十年来，头一回提前下课。
story.en:
"It can," said Xiaoman.

The whole hall was taken aback; so was Master Chu. It was a while before he said, "…How?"

"Go back for more," said Xiaoman.

The hall laughed again, only this time the laughter ran a little differently: the front rows turned to look at him like a boy talking nonsense; the mixed roots in the back didn't turn, only bent their heads, shoulders twitching. Xiaoman sat down, and the token on his chest went hot; a sleepy, impatient voice said in his ear: "…Who's making that racket?" He ducked his head. "The master says mixed roots are skimmers." The voice snorted. "What does he know." The token went cold. Xiaoman hid his mouth in his sleeve, shoulders shaking. Sun Ergou thought he'd been scolded to tears, patted him twice on the back and whispered, "Don't worry. I'm the hole at the bottom of the skimmer."

But Master Chu wouldn't let those words go. He rapped his ruler on the desk. "Draw it a few more times? In the *Liezi* there's a Foolish Old Man, near ninety, who resented two great mountains blocking his door and set his sons and grandsons carrying earth away basket by basket. A clever old man called the Wise Elder laughed at him: he couldn't even pull up one blade of grass on that mountain. Gentlemen, was the Wise Elder right?" The front rows chorused, "Right!" Master Chu said, "Therefore, in all things, first measure your strength. A skimmer is a skimmer."

A hand went up in the back row. Xiaoman stood. "Master, and then? The Foolish Old Man — did he dig the mountains flat in the end?"

Master Chu's beard stopped tilting. The end of the story he knew, of course: the Old Man said, when I die there are my sons, and sons have grandsons, sons and grandsons without end, and the mountains will grow no higher; moved by his sincerity, the Lord of Heaven sent two giants to carry the mountains away. He read it out by rote, very fast. "…So — the gods helped." Xiaoman said, "He still had to dig first. If he hadn't dug, how would the gods have known?"

No one laughed. Master Chu stood there a long while. "…That will be all for today." In thirty years it was the first time he had ended a lesson early.
